chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Goodwin's tribute to Lovett's steady time
summary: Goodwin says Lovett plays like a metronome and will not budge from the tempo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well here's the tribute that I myself would like to pay to Baby Lovett.

I played with Lovett about five years, big band, we were on the road traveling. He is one of the few drummers, you know, that I've played with, you know, he's just like a metronome. He sets a tempo --
-- and you can do whatever you want to do. He's going to --
Be there when you come back.
-- hold you right in tow. There won't be any -- you can run off if you want to but you'll be out there by yourself.

He wouldn't give an inch, you know. There's no way that he's going to follow you. He's going to keep that same beat but after a while I imagine the guy that would be off, when -- well he'd come back to what he was doing because he's not going to budge. See, this is what makes him a great drummer. This is what makes him the way he is.
